newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 24.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- Embattled Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates was at the centre of another storm last night when it was discovered he was not at Dublin Airport when the controversial Russian beef deal was signed.
- A top cabinet committee begins today to tackle what some ministers call a "cancer-like" growth in Exchequer spending.
- Dublin crinimal and self-confessed prime suspect in the murder of Irish crime journalist John Gilligan was refused bail by a Lonndon court on Wednesday.
- Irish insurer VHI clashed with private hospitals and consultants over claims that up to 20,000 unprocessed claims were responsible for hospitals' cash flow problems.
- Chain of theme restaurants, Planet Hollyhood, is in negotiations to open its first outlet in Dublin city centre.
- Second Irish mobile phone licencee Esat Digifone has awarded a three-year contract to run its directory enquiry service to new company Conduit Ireland.
- UK-based mortgage business Capital Home Loans, which was acquired by Irish Permanent for 12.6 million Irish pounds on Wednesday, recorded net profits of about 500,000 Irish pounds in 1995.
- The three political parties in Ireland's ruling coalition government have discussed the prospect of holding a general election in October 1997.
- A new law to protect the public against invasion of privacy and surveillance has been recommended by the Law Reform Commission.
- The Irish stock exchange will meet CountyGlen on Friday to decide whether it will grant it another time extension so that it can meet the requirements to have its suspension lifted.
- Irish property firm Power Corporation, which owes banks more than 190 million Irish pounds, is likely to be put into receivership within the next few days.
- A record level of investment from multinationals was attracted to Northern Ireland with the creation of 5,678 jobs in 1995, the Industrial Development Board said on Thursday.
- Yeoman International has purchased the business and assets of glass firm Tipperary Crystal for an undislcosed sum.
